    Sky Viewer

    • Drag the sky to look around. Scroll to zoom in and out (or pinch on a touchscreen).
    • Click a star or planet for details. Double-click to centre it.
    • Arrow keys pan, +/− zoom, Space pauses or resumes time.
    • Toggles: C lines, V constellation names, L labels, G alt/az grid, Q RA/Dec grid, H ground, A atmosphere.
    • The date and time are in your computer's time zone. UTC is shown under the clock.
    • With Atmosphere on, the sky brightens with the Sun, twilight hides faint stars, and stars dim near the horizon. Turn it off to see every star at any hour.

    Sky Viewer is open source: source code on GitHub · demo video · build report. In this web version, "Use my current location" is unavailable, so search for a city or type coordinates instead.

    Positions come from astronomy-engine. Stars are corrected for precession, nutation and atmospheric refraction. The Sun, Moon and planets also include light-time, aberration and parallax. Stars come from the Hipparcos/Yale Bright Star catalogs (via d3-celestial), down to magnitude 6.
